This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by the Hong Kong Observatory in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the Hong Kong Observatory, specifically the "Absolute Daily Max (deg. C)" the specified date once information is finalized in the relevant "Daily Extract", available here: https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/cis/climat.htm

This market can not resolve until data for this date has been published.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures in Celsius to one decimal place (eg, 9.1°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is initially published for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Hong Kong Observatory short-range guidance for August 13 projects a 27–33°C range under sunny periods with isolated showers, establishing 33°C as the market favorite at 44.5% implied probability. This aligns with above-normal seasonal temperatures and lingering effects from the recent heatwave that produced a record 36.8°C on August 9. Ensemble models show modest spread around peak readings, with cloud cover and convection introducing uncertainty that caps higher outcomes like 34°C at 28%. Traders weigh these factors against climatological August averages near 31–32°C, anticipating refined model runs and updated HKO briefings to refine resolution odds ahead of the daily maximum observation.

**Persistent subtropical high pressure and southerly flow are sustaining hot, mostly sunny conditions over Central Texas, positioning 100–101°F as the leading outcome for Austin’s August 13 high at 59% implied probability.** 

National Weather Service guidance and model consensus project a daily maximum near 101°F under this ridge, consistent with mid-August climatology where average highs reach 97–99°F but frequently climb to 100–102°F during heat-dome episodes. Limited cloud cover and dry air aloft will promote strong daytime heating, while light southerly winds add modest moisture without significantly capping temperatures. Recent forecasts show little day-to-day change from the August 12 pattern, keeping the 102–103°F bin at a distant 22.5% and lower bins below 13%. New NWS model runs or any unexpected convective development remain the main variables that could shift these market-implied odds before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models and Israel Meteorological Service guidance currently favor a daily maximum of 32–33 °C in Tel Aviv on August 14 under a persistent subtropical high-pressure ridge, clear skies, and light westerly flow. This places the outcome slightly above the mid-August climatological average of roughly 30–32 °C while remaining within the typical envelope for the season. Latest guidance from sources such as AccuWeather, timeanddate, and BBC Weather shows minimal day-to-day variability through the period, with no strong signals for intensification or cooling from Atlantic or Mediterranean influences. Trader positioning around 33 °C (56 %) versus 32 °C (33.5 %) reflects uncertainty in exact peak timing and potential urban heat-island contributions at official stations, while lower probabilities for 34 °C or higher acknowledge the limited upside in current ensemble spreads. Final model updates and real-time observations before peak heating are expected to tighten the range.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and GFS models indicate a persistent subtropical high-pressure ridge over northern Italy, supporting peak temperatures of 34–36 °C in Milan on August 14. These runs show limited day-to-day variability and place the most likely maximum near 35 °C, consistent with the market’s leading implied probabilities. Above-normal 850 hPa thicknesses and minimal cloud cover or precipitation are reinforcing the warm signal, though slight model spread in boundary-layer moisture keeps 34 °C and 36 °C as plausible alternatives. No significant synoptic changes have emerged in the past 48 hours, and climatological August extremes for the city rarely exceed 37 °C under similar setups. Updated model cycles and local observations through August 13 will provide the next key data points for traders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon flows from the Arabian Sea continue to deliver substantial moisture and cloud cover over Karachi, suppressing daytime maxima and positioning 32–33°C as the market's leading outcomes for the August 14 high. Official climatological data place the city's August average high near 31–32°C, with frequent convective activity and high humidity limiting radiative heating. Recent Pakistan Meteorological Department outlooks highlight sustained monsoon conditions through mid-August, consistent with model guidance showing limited clearing that would otherwise allow temperatures to climb into the mid-30s. Traders weigh these atmospheric patterns against historical analogs, where peak readings rarely exceed 34°C under similar late-summer regimes, while any unexpected break in cloud cover could shift probabilities toward slightly warmer bins.
